finding: hx-button.styles.ts line 133 uses `color: var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6b7280)` on the close button without a component-level token, breaking the three-tier token cascade. The value is consumed directly from the semantic tier, depriving consumers of a theming hook.
recommendation: Replace `color: var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6b7280)` with `color: var(--hx-dialog-close-btn-color, var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6b7280))`. Note: this defect is in hx-dialog.styles.ts not hx-button.styles.ts — see separate dialog record.

finding: Transition shorthand `var(--hx-transition-fast, 150ms ease)` collapses duration and easing into one token. The architecture requires separate `--hx-duration-*` and `--hx-easing-*` tokens, making it impossible for consumers to independently tune duration vs easing on this component.
recommendation: Split into `var(--hx-duration-fast, 150ms) var(--hx-easing-default, ease)` and ensure `--hx-duration-fast` and `--hx-easing-default` are defined in the token package.

finding: hx-button uses `hx-size` as the attribute name (`attribute: 'hx-size'`) but the reflected property is `size`. This inconsistency persists across hx-button, hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-switch, hx-checkbox, hx-slider, hx-number-input, and hx-toggle-button. The attribute name breaks convention — the `hx-` prefix on attributes is reserved for component-scoped properties like `hx-href`, not for common shared properties like size.
recommendation: Either standardize to attribute `size` across all components, or document the `hx-size` convention explicitly in CLAUDE.md as an intentional collision-avoidance strategy. The current state is undocumented inconsistency.

finding: In `updated()`, when the variant is invalid, `this.variant = 'primary'` is set directly inside the update cycle. This triggers a second synchronous update cycle. The correct pattern is to set the corrected value in `willUpdate()` before the render, preventing double-render.
recommendation: Move the variant validation from `updated()` into `willUpdate()`. The guard `changedProperties.has('variant')` works identically in both hooks.

finding: The `hx-click` event detail type `{ originalEvent: MouseEvent }` exposes a raw DOM event cross-component boundary. In composed event trees, the originalEvent's `target` will be retargeted and its `composedPath()` will be scoped to shadow DOM. Consumers using `detail.originalEvent.target` will receive the shadow host, not the inner button, creating confusing debugging.
recommendation: Document explicitly in the `@fires` JSDoc that `detail.originalEvent.target` is shadow-retargeted. Consider whether passing the original event as detail is necessary at all — `bubbles: true, composed: true` already propagates the event.

finding: hx-dialog.styles.ts line 133 hardcodes `color: var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6b7280)` on `.dialog__close-btn` without a component-level token. Line 145 uses `color: var(--hx-color-neutral-900)` and `background-color: var(--hx-color-neutral-100)` on hover with no component token and no hardcoded fallback. Missing fallbacks violates the three-tier cascade requirement.
recommendation: Add `--hx-dialog-close-btn-color` and `--hx-dialog-close-btn-hover-bg` component tokens with semantic fallbacks: `color: var(--hx-dialog-close-btn-color, var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6b7280))`

finding: hx-dialog.styles.ts line 133 uses `font-size: var(--hx-font-size-xl, 1.25rem)` on `.dialog__close-btn` without a component-level token. The close button font size cannot be themed without introducing global token overrides.
recommendation: Introduce `--hx-dialog-close-btn-size` token: `font-size: var(--hx-dialog-close-btn-size, var(--hx-font-size-xl, 1.25rem))`

finding: hx-dialog extends `LitElement` directly rather than `HelixElement`. All other major interactive components (hx-button, hx-select, hx-tabs, hx-textarea) extend `HelixElement` which provides `_internals`, `_onFormReset`, and base lifecycle consistency. hx-dialog's divergence from the base class pattern means it does not participate in any future HelixElement enhancements.
recommendation: Evaluate whether hx-dialog should extend HelixElement. If dialog intentionally opts out of form association, document that decision with a code comment referencing the architectural decision.

finding: hx-dialog.styles.ts line 141 renders the close button using `::before { content: '×' }` — the multiplication sign (×) is rendered as text content. This is read by some screen readers as 'times' or 'multiplication sign' even though `aria-label` is present. The aria-label is on the button correctly, but the `×` character leaks into the accessibility tree in certain AT configurations where CSS content is exposed.
recommendation: Replace the CSS `content: '×'` approach with an inline SVG icon with `aria-hidden='true'` (like other close buttons in the library, e.g. hx-alert's close button). This eliminates the AT ambiguity entirely.

finding: hx-dialog's `_openDialog()` method at line 305 calls `this.updateComplete.then()` to cache focusable elements and focus the first one, but `_isTransitioning` is set to `false` inside that promise. If the dialog is immediately closed before the promise resolves (e.g., programmatic `close()` on the same tick), `_isTransitioning` will be set to `false` after the close sequence has already completed, leaving `_isTransitioning` in an incorrect state and potentially breaking the guard on the next open/close cycle.
recommendation: Cancel the pending promise on close, or check `this.open` inside the `updateComplete.then()` callback before setting `_isTransitioning = false` and attempting focus.

finding: hx-dialog.styles.ts uses `display: contents` on `:host`. This is correct for allowing the dialog to participate in parent layout, but `display: contents` is known to have accessibility tree flattening issues in older Safari (pre-15.4) where the host element is removed from the accessibility tree entirely. For a modal dialog component in a healthcare context, this is a patient-safety-adjacent risk.
recommendation: Document the Safari <15.4 limitation in the component JSDoc. Consider using `display: block` with `contain: none` as an alternative if Safari support is required below 15.4.

finding: hx-select exposes `open` as a public reflected property (`@property({ type: Boolean, reflect: true })`). The dropdown open/close state is implementation-internal UX state, not a stable API surface. Reflecting it as an attribute means that attribute-observing frameworks (Drupal behaviors, MutationObserver consumers) will see spurious attribute churn on every dropdown interaction. This is a design boundary violation.
recommendation: Change `open` to `@state()` private `_open` and remove `reflect: true`. Expose `show()` and `hide()` methods for programmatic control. If external state reading is required, expose a `readonly open` getter.

finding: The global HTMLElementEventMap for `hx-change` is declared as `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>`. This union type is wrong for hx-select: hx-select only ever dispatches `{ value: string }`, never `{ checked: boolean; value: string }`. The union type leaks from hx-switch/hx-checkbox into the hx-select event map, creating a false impression that select can emit a checked field.
recommendation: Each component should declare its own narrowly-typed event in its own module's `HTMLElementEventMap`. The `hx-change` event on hx-select should be `CustomEvent<{ value: string }>` only. Create separate event map augmentations per component.

finding: hx-select renders ARIA attributes (`aria-hidden`, `aria-label`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`) on the hidden native `<select>` element at lines 716-721. The native select has `aria-hidden='true'` at line 714, making all other ARIA attributes on it meaningless — aria-hidden completely removes an element from the accessibility tree, so AT will never read those attributes. This is wasted markup and may confuse automated auditors.
recommendation: Remove `aria-label`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, and `aria-required` from the hidden native select. It should only have `tabindex='-1'`, `aria-hidden='true'`, `?required`, `?disabled`, and `name`.

finding: hx-select's `connectedCallback` at line 218 is a no-op body: `super.connectedCallback()` and nothing else. This adds noise — an empty override that provides no information to the reader about intentional behavior. Either remove it or add a comment explaining why it exists.
recommendation: Remove the `override connectedCallback()` entirely. The `super.connectedCallback()` call is implicit in Lit's lifecycle when the method is not overridden.

finding: In `_handleSlotChange()`, when `this.value` is already set and options are parsed, `this._select.value = this.value` is called (line 388). However if the value does not match any option, the native select silently resets to its first option. This means `this.value` and `this._select.value` can silently diverge without any warning, corrupting form submission values.
recommendation: After `this._select.value = this.value`, verify that `this._select.value === this.value`. If they diverge, either emit a `devWarn` or set `this.value = this._select.value` to restore consistency.

finding: hx-switch renders `hasError` in `describedBy` at line 290 using `hasError || this._hasErrorSlot` for the condition, but `hasError` is computed as `!!this.error` at line 277 (not including `_hasErrorSlot`). This means when error is provided only via the error slot (no `error` property), the error container class `switch--error` is NOT applied to the container, but the errorId IS included in `describedBy`. The error styling and ARIA linkage are out of sync.
recommendation: Change the `hasError` definition from `!!this.error` to `!!this.error || this._hasErrorSlot` to ensure visual error state and ARIA state are always consistent, matching the pattern used in hx-text-input, hx-select, and hx-checkbox.

finding: hx-switch does not expose `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` as public methods, but hx-checkbox, hx-select, and hx-radio-group all do. The omission creates an inconsistent form API surface across all form-associated components. Consumers using a generic form validation loop that calls `checkValidity()` on all form elements will fail silently on hx-switch instances.
recommendation: Add `checkValidity(): boolean { return this._internals.checkValidity(); }` and `reportValidity(): boolean { return this._internals.reportValidity(); }` to match the form API contract of all peer components.

finding: hx-checkbox uses `requestAnimationFrame` inside `updated()` at line 178 to defer `_announcedError` state assignment. Setting `@state` properties inside a rAF callback from within `updated()` triggers a second asynchronous render cycle outside of Lit's batch update mechanism. This is not a Lit anti-pattern per se, but `_announcedError` being `@state` means every rAF callback will schedule a full render. In rapid error-change scenarios (form validation loops), this produces N rAF-deferred renders.
recommendation: This implementation is deliberately chosen for WCAG 4.1.3 re-announcement behavior. If retained, add a comment citing the specific WCAG success criterion and AT behavior being addressed (already partially present). If performance is a concern, throttle via a flag that prevents stacking rAF calls.

finding: hx-checkbox wraps the input in a `<label>` element and also adds a `@click` handler directly on the label at line 316. The click handler calls `_handleChange()` which manually toggles `checked`. The native label-for association already triggers the input's click event, meaning a single user click fires BOTH the label's `@click` AND the input's native change event. The `@click` on the input at line 333 calls `e.preventDefault()` and `e.stopPropagation()`, attempting to suppress the double-fire, but this approach is fragile and creates a custom state machine on top of native behavior.
recommendation: Remove the `@click` handler from the `<label>` element. Use only the native `change` event on the `<input>` to detect state changes. The label-for relationship handles click-to-focus and click-to-toggle natively. The current preventDefault chain is a maintenance liability.

finding: hx-tabs exposes `label` as a public property with `reflect: true`, but the default value is empty string `''`. When `label` is empty, the render at line 479 falls back to `'Tabs'` as the aria-label, bypassing the empty-string check. However in `firstUpdated()` at line 201, the devWarn fires when `label === ''`. The component thus emits a warning AND renders a fallback — the fallback is never documented as the behavior, creating a confusing contract. Consumers will see the warning but not understand that 'Tabs' is silently used.
recommendation: Either document `'Tabs'` as the explicit default value in the JSDoc and initialize `label = 'Tabs'` to make the default authoritative, or remove the silent fallback from render() and require the consumer to always set a label.

finding: hx-tabs `updated()` at line 231 checks `(changedProperties as Map<PropertyKey, unknown>).has('_activePanel')`. Casting changedProperties and checking for a private `@state()` property is unnecessary — Lit passes all changed reactive properties (both `@property` and `@state`) in changedProperties. The cast to `Map<PropertyKey, unknown>` suggests the developer was unsure of the type. `changedProperties.has('_activePanel' as keyof HelixTabs)` is the type-safe way.
recommendation: Replace `(changedProperties as Map<PropertyKey, unknown>).has('_activePanel')` with `changedProperties.has('_activePanel' as keyof typeof this)`. Alternatively, move `_updateTabsAndPanels()` to the end of `_activateTab()` and remove the `updated()` override entirely, since `_activateTab` is the only thing that changes `_activePanel`.

finding: hx-tabs.styles.ts uses a hardcoded `12rem` as the fallback value for `--hx-tabs-vertical-width` at line 61. The `12rem` value is not mapped to any `--hx-size-*` or `--hx-space-*` token, violating the no-hardcoded-values policy. Even fallback values in token expressions should reference the token system.
recommendation: Replace `var(--hx-tabs-vertical-width, 12rem)` with `var(--hx-tabs-vertical-width, var(--hx-size-48, 12rem))` once `--hx-size-48` is confirmed in the token set, or define a semantic token `--hx-sidebar-width-sm` to semantically anchor the value.

finding: hx-tabs.styles.ts hardcodes `1px` as the border-width fallback (`var(--hx-tabs-border-width, 1px)`) at line 32. The `--hx-border-width-thin` token exists in the system (used in hx-button, hx-dialog) and should be the second-tier fallback here.
recommendation: Change to `var(--hx-tabs-border-width, var(--hx-border-width-thin, 1px))` to follow the three-tier cascade pattern used consistently elsewhere.

finding: hx-alert uses `querySelector` inside `firstUpdated()` and `disconnectedCallback()` to find slots (lines 200-214 and 188-195). The Lit `@query` decorator exists precisely for this pattern. Using `querySelector` in lifecycle hooks is the anti-pattern the decorator was introduced to eliminate — it is imperative DOM querying inside a declarative component.
recommendation: Replace the manual `querySelector` slot lookups with `@query('slot[name=actions]') private _actionsSlot` and `@query('slot[name=title]') private _titleSlot`. Wire the slot change handlers directly in `render()` using `@slotchange` binding, which is the correct Lit pattern used by all peer components.

finding: hx-alert stores handler references as `_actionsSlotChangeHandler` and `_titleSlotChangeHandler` properties (lines 135-137) as nullable function fields because it uses `querySelector` in `firstUpdated()`. This entire pattern is unnecessary complexity. It exists only because the slots are not wired with `@slotchange` in the template. The `disconnectedCallback` then manually removes these listeners, which duplicates what Lit's event binding system handles automatically.
recommendation: Remove `_actionsSlotChangeHandler` and `_titleSlotChangeHandler` fields entirely. Wire slot change events declaratively in `render()` with `@slotchange=${this._handleActionsSlotChange}`. This eliminates the manual add/remove listener pattern and removes approximately 25 lines of lifecycle boilerplate.

finding: hx-alert uses `hx-close` as its dismiss event name, but hx-dialog also uses `hx-close` for its close event. These are semantically different operations on different component types, but using the same event name across components means a parent element listening for `hx-close` bubbling up cannot distinguish between an alert being dismissed vs a dialog being closed without inspecting `event.target`.
recommendation: Rename the alert dismiss event to `hx-dismiss` to differentiate it from hx-dialog's `hx-close`. Update the `@fires` JSDoc and `HTMLElementEventMap` accordingly. This is a breaking change that should be versioned.

finding: hx-alert.styles.ts line 46 uses `font-size: var(--hx-font-size-sm, 0.875rem)` directly on `.alert` without a component-level `--hx-alert-font-size` token. Consumers cannot theme the alert font size without overriding the global semantic token, which affects all other consumers of `--hx-font-size-sm`.
recommendation: Add `@cssprop [--hx-alert-font-size=var(--hx-font-size-sm)]` and use `font-size: var(--hx-alert-font-size, var(--hx-font-size-sm, 0.875rem))` in the stylesheet.

finding: hx-alert.styles.ts line 149 uses `var(--hx-transition-fast, 150ms ease)` — the same collapsed transition shorthand issue as hx-button. Additionally this component-level transition has no component-level override token, meaning consumers cannot slow down the alert dismissal animation without affecting all components using `--hx-transition-fast`.
recommendation: Add `--hx-alert-transition-duration` and use proper two-token split: `var(--hx-alert-transition-duration, var(--hx-duration-fast, 150ms)) var(--hx-easing-default, ease)`.

finding: hx-slider's `valueText` property maps to the `aria-valuetext` attribute (`attribute: 'aria-valuetext'`). Declaring a property with an `aria-*` attribute name shadows ARIAMixin's native `ariaValueText` property. This creates two competing property paths for the same ARIA attribute. In browsers that implement ARIAMixin, `this.ariaValueText` and `this.valueText` would map to different internal slots. This is the same class of bug that hx-dialog explicitly works around (lines 91-93 of hx-dialog.ts).
recommendation: Rename `valueText` to a non-ARIA attribute name (e.g., `value-text` attribute, `valueText` property) and set it on the inner `<input>` directly, or follow the hx-dialog pattern of observing the attribute through `observedAttributes` and `attributeChangedCallback` without declaring a shadowing property.

finding: hx-slider.styles.ts declares `--hx-slider-thumb-border-width=2px` in the CEM docs but this token is used directly as `2px` in the styles with no component token reference. The `2px` fallback is not bridged through a `--hx-border-width-*` semantic token.
recommendation: Review hx-slider.styles.ts to ensure `--hx-slider-thumb-border-width` references the semantic `--hx-border-width-thin` as its fallback rather than a raw px value.

finding: hx-slider's `updated()` at lines 268-281 clamps `this.value` when it falls outside `[min, max]` and then `return`s early. This return prevents `setFormValue` from being called when a clamp occurs. The `setFormValue` call at line 278 only runs when `clamped === this.value`. If the value was clamped, the form value is NOT updated to the clamped value — the form retains the out-of-range value until the next update cycle triggered by the recursive property set.
recommendation: Move `this._internals.setFormValue(String(this.value))` to AFTER the clamp assignment, before the `return`, so the form value always matches the clamped component value immediately.

finding: hx-number-input.styles.ts uses `var(--hx-opacity-disabled)` at line 9 WITHOUT a hardcoded fallback. If `--hx-opacity-disabled` is not defined in the consuming context (e.g., a Drupal instance that hasn't loaded the token stylesheet), the opacity property silently computes to the initial value `1`, making disabled inputs appear fully enabled. All other components use `var(--hx-opacity-disabled, 0.5)`.
recommendation: Add the fallback: `opacity: var(--hx-opacity-disabled, 0.5)` to match the pattern in hx-select, hx-radio-group, and hx-textarea.

finding: hx-number-input.styles.ts lines 20-56 use tokens without hardcoded fallbacks throughout: `var(--hx-space-1)`, `var(--hx-font-size-sm)`, `var(--hx-font-weight-medium)`, `var(--hx-line-height-normal)`, `var(--hx-border-width-thin)`, `var(--hx-transition-fast)`, `var(--hx-font-weight-bold)`, `var(--hx-color-neutral-700)`. All peer components (hx-textarea, hx-select) include hardcoded fallbacks. hx-number-input is the only form component that relies entirely on the token stylesheet being loaded.
recommendation: Add hardcoded fallbacks to all token references in hx-number-input.styles.ts. Example: `var(--hx-space-1, 0.25rem)`, `var(--hx-font-size-sm, 0.875rem)`, etc. This is a systematic defect across the entire stylesheet.

finding: hx-number-input's `size` property uses `attribute: 'hx-size'` but does NOT include `reflect: true` (line 154), unlike hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-switch, hx-checkbox, hx-slider, and hx-toggle-button which all reflect `size`. This means CSS selectors like `:host([hx-size='lg'])` do not work for hx-number-input, but they do for all peer components. Inconsistency in reflect behavior breaks CSS-based theming patterns.
recommendation: Add `reflect: true` to the `size` property decorator: `@property({ type: String, attribute: 'hx-size', reflect: true })`.

finding: hx-number-input documents `@csspart error-message` in its JSDoc, but the peer form components (hx-text-input, hx-textarea, hx-checkbox, hx-select) all use `@csspart error` for the error message container. The inconsistent part name `error-message` vs `error` means CSS theming consumers cannot write a single selector targeting error states across all form inputs.
recommendation: Rename the part from `error-message` to `error` to match the part naming used across all peer form components. Update the `part='error-message'` attribute in the render template to `part='error'`.

finding: hx-toggle-button uses `console.warn` directly at line 145 instead of the `devWarn` utility used by every other component in the library. This means: 1) The warning appears in production builds when `devWarn` strips them. 2) The warning message format is inconsistent with all other component warnings. 3) It cannot be silenced by the same mechanism consumers use to suppress devWarn output.
recommendation: Replace `console.warn('[hx-toggle-button] ...')` with `devWarn('hx-toggle-button', '...')`. Import `devWarn` from `'../../utils/dev-warn.js'` as done in hx-button, hx-select, hx-slider, hx-number-input, and hx-tabs.

finding: hx-toggle-button's `label` property (line 102) conflicts with the semantic meaning of the `label` property in hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-switch, hx-checkbox, hx-slider, hx-number-input, and hx-radio-group — where `label` always maps to the visible field label text. In hx-toggle-button, `label` maps to `aria-label` on the inner button, which is an accessible name override, not a visible label. This is a naming inconsistency.
recommendation: Rename hx-toggle-button's `label` property to `accessible-name` (attribute) / `accessibleName` (property), OR rename it to `aria-label` consistent with how hx-text-input and hx-select declare their ARIA name override property. The current `label` name creates false API alignment with form field labels.

finding: hx-toggle-button's `_syncFormValue` is called from BOTH `updated()` and `_handleClick()`. In `_handleClick()`, `this.pressed = !this.pressed` triggers a reactive update, which calls `updated()`, which calls `_syncFormValue()`. Then `_handleClick()` also calls `this._syncFormValue()` explicitly after the assignment. This means `setFormValue` is called twice on every click.
recommendation: Remove the explicit `this._syncFormValue()` call from `_handleClick()` at line 216. The reactive update cycle from `this.pressed = !this.pressed` guarantees `updated()` fires, which already calls `_syncFormValue()`.

finding: hx-breadcrumb uses imperative DOM manipulation throughout: `document.createElement()` in `_applyCollapse()` (line 235), `firstItem.after()` (line 253), `this._ellipsisItem.remove()` (line 264). This pattern entirely bypasses Lit's rendering system. Changes to the light DOM made this way will not be tracked by Lit and may be clobbered on the next re-render, or may persist after property changes that should hide the ellipsis.
recommendation: This is architecturally the correct approach for a component that manages light-DOM children that it did not create, given that Lit's render() only controls shadow DOM. However, the coupling between `_ellipsisItem` mutation and Lit's update cycle is fragile. Document explicitly in the class-level JSDoc that this component uses imperative light-DOM mutation as an intentional pattern, and add a `_ellipsisItem` cleanup in `disconnectedCallback` to prevent memory leaks.

finding: hx-breadcrumb's JSON-LD injection at `_updateJsonLd()` uses `document.head.appendChild()` at line 336. The component's own JSDoc (lines 78-87) correctly warns that this is problematic in Drupal. However, there is no guard preventing JSON-LD script injection during SSR (server-side rendering) where `document.head` may not exist. The `typeof document === 'undefined'` guard exists for `_applyCollapse()` but is missing from the `document.head.appendChild()` call path in `_updateJsonLd()`.
recommendation: The `typeof document === 'undefined'` guard at line 323 fires before `document.head.appendChild()`, so this is actually guarded correctly. However the guard comment says 'Guard for SSR' but then uses `document.getElementById()` on line 330 which could still fail if document exists but head does not (e.g., in a document fragment). Tighten to check `typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.head`.

finding: hx-card uses `hx-href` and `hx-label` as attribute names (lines 71 and 79) to avoid conflict with native HTML `href`. However, this establishes a one-off `hx-` prefix convention for properties that are NOT shared across components — the prefix is not used for `href` in hx-button (which uses `href` directly). The asymmetry between hx-button's `href` and hx-card's `hx-href` is a consumer-facing API inconsistency.
recommendation: Document the intentional difference in CLAUDE.md: `hx-href` is used on hx-card because the card is a `<div>`, not an `<a>`, and the `hx-` prefix signals this is a custom behavior, not a native attribute passthrough. Without this documentation, consumers will assume the APIs are equivalent and be surprised.

finding: hx-card renders `role='link'` on a `<div>` when interactive (hx-href is set). The `role='link'` requires the element to navigate on activation. hx-card dispatches `hx-click` but does NOT perform navigation itself — it relies on the consumer to handle navigation in the event listener. ARIA role requirements state that `role='link'` must have a keyboard-accessible activation that performs the navigation the role implies. A card that fires an event but does not navigate fails this requirement if the consumer forgets to implement navigation.
recommendation: Either: 1) Render an actual `<a>` element wrapping the card content with `href` set to `this.href` (the correct ARIA pattern), or 2) Change the role to `role='button'` since the component dispatches a custom event rather than navigating. If keeping `role='link'`, document that consumer MUST implement navigation in the event handler, and add a devWarn when hx-href is set but no event listener is attached (not currently detectable, so option 1 or 2 is strongly preferred).

finding: hx-textarea.styles.ts line 113 hardcodes `resize: vertical` in `.field__textarea` without any token. The resize behavior is controlled via the `resize` property/attribute reflected in `:host([resize='...'])` selectors, but the base value of `resize: vertical` has no theming hook. Consumers cannot change the default resize behavior via CSS custom property.
recommendation: This is an acceptable design choice since `resize` is exposed as a component property with full attribute reflection. Document in JSDoc that the resize behavior is controlled via the `resize` attribute, not CSS custom properties.

finding: hx-textarea.styles.ts uses `--hx-input-*` CSS custom property names (lines 36-77). The component is `hx-textarea` but its tokens are prefixed `--hx-input-*`. This means hx-textarea shares token namespace with hx-text-input. A consumer overriding `--hx-input-bg` to theme the textarea will simultaneously theme all text inputs. The two components should have independent component-level token namespaces.
recommendation: Introduce `--hx-textarea-*` tokens for hx-textarea-specific theming (e.g., `--hx-textarea-bg`, `--hx-textarea-border-color`) that fall back to `--hx-input-*` as semantic defaults. This preserves backwards compatibility while enabling independent theming: `var(--hx-textarea-bg, var(--hx-input-bg, var(--hx-color-neutral-0, #ffffff)))`.

finding: hx-textarea.styles.ts lines 155-157 use `var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6c757d)` for `.field__counter` color and lines 178-179 use `var(--hx-color-neutral-500, #6c757d)` for `.field__help-text` color without component-level tokens. Both values bypass the three-tier cascade.
recommendation: Add `--hx-textarea-counter-color` and `--hx-textarea-help-text-color` component tokens with semantic fallbacks. The `--hx-input-*` or `--hx-textarea-*` namespace should be used.

finding: hx-radio-group renders a `<fieldset>` with `role='radiogroup'` at line 485. The `<fieldset>` element already has an implicit ARIA role of `group`. Adding an explicit `role='radiogroup'` on a `<fieldset>` overrides the implicit `group` role with `radiogroup`. While both roles are semantically appropriate for a radio group, the combination of native `<fieldset>` with explicit `role='radiogroup'` may cause redundant role announcement in some AT configurations ('group, radiogroup'). The native `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` pattern does not require an explicit ARIA role.
recommendation: Remove `role='radiogroup'` from the `<fieldset>` element. The native `<fieldset>` provides group semantics implicitly. If radiogroup role is required for specific AT support, use a non-semantic element (e.g., `<div role='radiogroup'>`) instead of adding the role to the native `<fieldset>`.

finding: hx-radio-group's `hx-change` event at line 290 dispatches `{ value: string, checked: boolean }` where `checked` is always `true` — a radio selection always results in a checked state. The `checked` field is misleading because it implies a radio can be unchecked via this event, which is not possible in a single-select radio group. It also creates API inconsistency with hx-select's `hx-change` which is `{ value: string }` only.
recommendation: Remove the `checked: boolean` field from hx-radio-group's `hx-change` event detail. Emit only `{ value: string }` to match hx-select's contract and eliminate the always-true `checked` field.

finding: hx-radio-group's `updated()` only tracks `'value'` and `'disabled'` changes to call `_syncRadios()`. If a consumer programmatically adds or removes `hx-radio` children after initial render (common in dynamic Drupal forms), `_cachedRadios` is invalidated by `_handleSlotChange()` but `_syncRadios()` is called from the slot change handler only. If children are added imperatively via DOM manipulation (not via slot assignment), the cache is never invalidated.
recommendation: Document that programmatic light-DOM manipulation (outside slot assignment) requires calling an invalidation method. Add a `refresh()` public method that clears `_cachedRadios` and calls `_syncRadios()`, enabling consumers to explicitly trigger re-sync after imperative DOM changes.

finding: The global HTMLElementEventMap augmentation for hx-text-input at line 515 declares `hx-change` as `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>`. hx-text-input never emits `{ checked: boolean; value: string }`. This union type is a copy-paste defect from hx-checkbox/hx-switch and provides false type information to TypeScript consumers who type `event.detail.checked` and receive `undefined` at runtime instead of a type error.
recommendation: Change the hx-change event map entry for hx-text-input to `CustomEvent<{ value: string }>` only. Each component's global event map augmentation must be scoped to only the events that component actually emits.

finding: hx-text-input reflects `name` via `reflect: true` (line 126) but `value` does NOT reflect (line 84). hx-select reflects both `name` and `value`. hx-slider reflects `value` and `name`. hx-textarea reflects only `name`, not `value`. The inconsistency in which form fields reflect `value` makes it impossible to write consistent CSS selectors like `:host([value=''])` to detect empty state across all form components.
recommendation: Establish a library-wide policy: either all form components reflect `value` or none do. Given that hx-select and hx-slider reflect `value`, the policy should be to reflect consistently. Add `reflect: true` to the `value` property in hx-text-input and hx-textarea, or document why some components reflect value and others don't.

finding: hx-text-input's `_updateValidity()` at line 295 checks `this.value.length > 0` before validating minlength. This means a required field with a minlength constraint will NOT show a minlength error when the field is empty — it will show the `valueMissing` error instead. This is technically correct behavior (empty field → required error), but if `required` is false and the field has a minlength, submitting an empty value would pass validation even though an empty string arguably violates the spirit of minlength. Document this edge case.
recommendation: Add a JSDoc comment on `_updateValidity()` explaining that empty string is treated as 'no value' for minlength validation, consistent with HTML spec behavior where minlength only applies to non-empty values.

finding: hx-textarea exports both `HxTextarea` and `WcTextarea` (deprecated) type aliases at lines 541-544, as does hx-text-input (lines 520-523) and hx-checkbox (lines 397-400). However, hx-select exports via `export type { HelixSelect as HxSelect }` (line 764) syntax instead of `export type HxSelect = HelixSelect`. These two export patterns produce identical runtime behavior but different declaration file outputs. Inconsistency between named re-exports and type alias declarations will create noise in IDE autocomplete.
recommendation: Standardize all component type exports to use the same pattern. The `export type Hx... = Helix...` form (used in hx-textarea) is more readable. Update hx-select to match.

finding: hx-dialog.styles.ts uses `--hx-space-5`, `--hx-space-6`, `--hx-space-4`, `--hx-space-3`, `--hx-space-8` without hardcoded fallbacks throughout lines 97-174. The header padding `var(--hx-space-5) var(--hx-space-6)` has no pixel fallback. If the token stylesheet is not loaded, the dialog will have zero padding on all sections, making it visually broken.
recommendation: Add hardcoded fallbacks to all space tokens without them in hx-dialog.styles.ts. Minimum: `var(--hx-space-5, 1.25rem)`, `var(--hx-space-6, 1.5rem)`, `var(--hx-space-4, 1rem)`, `var(--hx-space-3, 0.75rem)`, `var(--hx-space-8, 2rem)`.

finding: hx-alert renders the title slot container (`.alert__title`) as `display: none` by default and toggles to `display: block` via the `alert__title--visible` class using `classMap` inside the template string: `class='alert__title ${this._hasTitle ? 'alert__title--visible' : ''}'`. This uses string interpolation inside a classMap context rather than the proper `classMap()` directive. While it works, it bypasses Lit's efficient DOM diffing for class updates.
recommendation: Replace the string-interpolated class on `.alert__title` div with `classMap({ 'alert__title': true, 'alert__title--visible': this._hasTitle })`. Same fix applies to `.alert__actions`. This ensures Lit only modifies the changed class, rather than replacing the entire class string.

finding: hx-slider's `updated()` at line 283 manually calls `this.setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true')` and `this.removeAttribute('aria-disabled')`. The `HelixElement` base class and `ARIAMixin` provide `ariaDisabled` as a property. Manually managing ARIA attributes via setAttribute/removeAttribute in updated() alongside a Lit element that may also manage these attributes creates a dual-write race condition.
recommendation: Use `this.ariaDisabled = this.disabled ? 'true' : null` instead of imperative setAttribute/removeAttribute calls. If the base class does not automatically sync `disabled` to `ariaDisabled`, use a `@property({ attribute: 'aria-disabled', reflect: true })` declarative override OR document why the imperative approach is necessary (e.g., ARIAMixin limitations).

finding: hx-card's JSDoc documents `@cssprop [--hx-card-image-aspect-ratio=16/9]` but the slash in `16/9` is not a valid CSS custom property value string in all contexts — it is valid in `aspect-ratio` but when written in JSDoc as a default it implies the raw string `16/9` is the fallback. The CEM @cssprop notation for default values should reflect what the browser actually uses.
recommendation: This is a documentation clarity issue, not a code defect. Change the JSDoc to `@cssprop [--hx-card-image-aspect-ratio] - Aspect ratio for the image slot (default: 16/9)` to avoid implying the raw CSS value in the bracket notation.

finding: hx-breadcrumb's `labelEllipsis` property (line 73) uses `@property({ attribute: 'label-ellipsis' })` without specifying `type: String`. The `@property()` decorator defaults to `type: String` when no type is specified, but explicit `type: String` is required by the project convention (demonstrated across all other string properties). Multiple properties across multiple components omit `type: String`: hx-select's `labelRequired` (line 180), `labelNoOptions` (line 186), hx-alert's `labelClose` (line 81), hx-slider's `valueText` is documented above.
recommendation: Add `type: String` to all `@property()` decorators that omit it. This is a library-wide convention enforcement issue, not just isolated to hx-breadcrumb. File: multiple components. The omission creates an implicit reliance on default behavior that should be explicit.

finding: hx-checkbox reflects `value` via `reflect: true` (line 98), but the default value is `'on'` — a string that reflects as the attribute `value='on'`. For checkboxes used without explicit value assignment, every instance will render `value='on'` in the DOM attribute, which adds visual noise in DOM inspectors and may confuse automated Drupal attribute scrapers that process form field attributes.
recommendation: Remove `reflect: true` from the `value` property unless there is a documented use case for CSS selectors targeting `:host([value='on'])`. Reflecting `value` on checkboxes is not standard HTML behavior — the native `<input type='checkbox'>` does not reflect its `value` attribute dynamically.

finding: hx-tabs' `_syncTabsAndPanels()` at lines 261-277 extracts the tab's text content to set `aria-label` on the panel. Text-node extraction with `.join('').trim()` strips all element structure. If a tab contains nested HTML (e.g., a badge with a count: `Patient Records 3`), the extracted text is `Patient Records3` without spacing. The resulting panel aria-label `'Patient Records3'` is semantically wrong.
recommendation: Filter only text nodes (nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE) for the label extraction and join with a space separator to prevent number concatenation: `.filter(n => n.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE).map(n => n.textContent?.trim()).filter(Boolean).join(' ')`.

finding: hx-radio-group.styles.ts uses `var(--hx-font-family-sans, sans-serif)` directly on the fieldset (line 26) without a component-level token. All peer form components (hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-textarea, hx-number-input) use a `--hx-*-font-family` component token that wraps the semantic token. hx-radio-group lacks this indirection.
recommendation: Add `--hx-radio-group-font-family` token to the `@cssprop` documentation and use it in styles: `font-family: var(--hx-radio-group-font-family, var(--hx-font-family-sans, sans-serif))`.

finding: hx-switch.ts exports `WcSwitch` and `HxSwitch` at lines 354-356, but the export order is `WcSwitch` first, `HxSwitch` second. Every other component puts the canonical current alias (`Hx*`) first and the deprecated alias (`Wc*`) second with a `@deprecated` tag. hx-switch has the order reversed and the `WcSwitch` export lacks a `@deprecated` JSDoc annotation unlike hx-checkbox and hx-textarea.
recommendation: Add `/** @deprecated Use HxSwitch instead. */` to the `WcSwitch` export and reorder so `HxSwitch` appears before `WcSwitch`. Match the pattern established in hx-checkbox and hx-textarea.

finding: hx-dialog.ts does not export a type alias (`HxDialog`) at module level. Every other substantive component (hx-button exports `HelixButton` via the class; hx-text-input exports `HxTextInput`; hx-textarea exports `HxTextarea`; hx-checkbox exports `HxCheckbox`) provides a type alias for consumers who prefer non-Helix-prefixed names. hx-dialog's omission means its consumer type is only `HelixDialog`, while all peers offer `Hx*`.
recommendation: Add `export type HxDialog = HelixDialog;` after the class declaration in hx-dialog.ts to establish consistency with all other component exports.

finding: hx-text-input's `@cssprop` documentation declares `[--hx-input-sm-font-size=0.875rem]` and `[--hx-input-lg-font-size=1.125rem]` (lines 50-51), but the semantic token fallback should reference `--hx-font-size-sm` and `--hx-font-size-lg` respectively. The hardcoded `0.875rem` and `1.125rem` as default values in CEM documentation bypass the semantic tier, misleading consumers into thinking these are fully independent values rather than aliases for the font-size token scale.
recommendation: Update CEM docs to `[--hx-input-sm-font-size=var(--hx-font-size-sm,0.875rem)]` and `[--hx-input-lg-font-size=var(--hx-font-size-lg,1.125rem)]` to document the full cascade. Verify the actual stylesheet uses the semantic token as the second-tier fallback.

finding: hx-card's `updated()` at lines 164-178 checks `changedProperties.has('href') || changedProperties.has('label')` to warn about missing accessible name. However `_headingText` is `@state()` and is updated asynchronously by the slot change handler. On first render, `href` may be set before `_headingText` is populated, triggering a spurious warning before the heading slot content has been read.
recommendation: Move the accessible-name check to `firstUpdated()` or add a guard that checks whether the component has fully initialized before emitting the warning. Alternatively, defer the check via `this.updateComplete.then(() => { /* check */ })` in `connectedCallback`.

finding: hx-breadcrumb's @cssprop for `--hx-breadcrumb-separator-content` documents the default value as `'/'` but in the component's stylesheet, the value must be CSS-quoted (i.e., the property value must be `"'/'"` not `"/"`). The @cssprop documentation does not indicate this quoting requirement, which will cause consumers to incorrectly set `--hx-breadcrumb-separator-content: >` and see no separator (the component's own JSDoc on lines 31-34 warns about this but the CEM @cssprop does not).
recommendation: Update the @cssprop notation to `@cssprop [--hx-breadcrumb-separator-content='/'] - Separator character. MUST be CSS-quoted: set as --hx-breadcrumb-separator-content: ">", not --hx-breadcrumb-separator-content: >.` so automated CEM documentation captures the constraint.

finding: The `hx-change` event detail shape is inconsistent across form components: hx-text-input emits `{ value: string }`, hx-checkbox emits `{ checked: boolean, value: string }`, hx-switch emits `{ checked: boolean, value: string }`, hx-select emits `{ value: string }`, hx-radio-group emits `{ value: string, checked: boolean }`, hx-slider emits `{ value: number }`, hx-number-input emits `{ value: number | null }`. Consumers building a unified form change handler must inspect `event.detail` structure to determine component type, defeating the purpose of a consistent event contract.
recommendation: Define a union type `HxChangeEventDetail` in a shared types file and document which components emit which variant. At minimum, establish a rule: boolean-selection components (checkbox, switch, radio) include `checked`, value-only components (text, select, textarea) do not. hx-radio-group emitting `{ value, checked: true }` should be changed to `{ value }` since `checked` is always `true`. Publish the event contract matrix in docs.

finding: hx-select.styles.ts at line 31 documents `--hx-select-chevron-size=0.5rem` as a CEM prop. The `0.5rem` value does not correspond to any `--hx-space-*` token (which would be `--hx-space-2` = 0.5rem). The lack of a semantic fallback means the chevron size is not in sync with the spacing scale if the spacing scale changes.
recommendation: Change to `var(--hx-select-chevron-size, var(--hx-space-2, 0.5rem))` to anchor the default to the spacing token scale.

finding: SUMMARY: Tier 2 review identified 50 findings across 15 components. Critical: 1 (systematic event detail type inconsistency). High: 19 (hx-alert querySelector anti-pattern, hx-select open property design, hx-number-input missing token fallbacks, hx-slider form value race, hx-dialog close button character content in AT, hx-dialog transition race, hx-card role=link without navigation, hx-radio-group fieldset+role redundancy, hx-toggle-button console.warn, hx-textarea token namespace collision, hx-select ARIA on aria-hidden element, hx-breadcrumb imperative DOM, hx-select native/custom state divergence, hx-select event map type contamination, hx-text-input event map type contamination, hx-dialog LitElement vs HelixElement, hx-alert event naming collision with hx-dialog). Medium: 22. Low: 8. Top 3 systemic defects: 1) hx-change event detail shapes are inconsistent across all form components (no shared contract), 2) hx-number-input uses tokens without hardcoded fallbacks throughout its entire stylesheet (breaks token-absent environments), 3) hx-textarea shares --hx-input-* token namespace with hx-text-input, preventing independent theming.
recommendation: Block merge until: 1) hx-change event detail types are normalized across all form components with a shared type definition, 2) hx-number-input.styles.ts adds hardcoded fallbacks to all token references, 3) hx-alert replaces querySelector pattern with @slotchange declarative bindings, 4) hx-select removes open from public reflected API, 5) hx-toggle-button replaces console.warn with devWarn.
